title: Normalized strict étale coefficient transport interfaces
statement: For a scheme T and commutative rings O,O′ with elements ell,mu, a ring homomorphism phi:O→O′ and a monotone index map r, a strict coefficient change consists of maps O/(ell^(r(n)+1))→O′/(mu^(n+1)) sending every quotient generator x to phi(x). On the actual strict module-system and unbounded derived categories [def-per-strict-etale-system-interfaces, def-pur-coefficient-system-image-data], a coefficient transport consists of exact additive ordinary extension after r, its levelwise tensor evaluation isomorphisms and tensor-unit maps, with successor compatibility, and its derived descent with its representative equation. Quotient comparisons retain the ordinary tensor-unit and derived universal-counit equations. For a geometric morphism, inverse-image transports retain the set-sheaf unit normalization and derived representative equation. For a compactification, compact-support transports consist of these open/proper inverse-image squares, their open/proper mates and their composite projection. Composition and identity identifications are fixed by tensor units and localization on complexes. These are precisely the existing definitions relocated unchanged from EtaleCoefficientSystemAdjoint; no existence result is part of the interface.
